# NL3xxx\: modules and the driver

The 51 codes of band 3. [Diagnostics](../diagnostics.md) says what a code promises and how a rule's fragment is matched.

## NL3001

```text
…--target: unsupported target `
```

**No program provokes it**: `--target: unsupported target` is a usage error (exit 2), not a diagnostic

## NL3010


[`nl3010_generic_redeclared.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl3010_generic_redeclared.ts):

```ts
// NL3010: two modules declaring one generic name. An instantiation is named
// after its template, so both would emit `@identity$i32` — the same collision
// the plain-function rule refuses, one namespace up. Two *packages* may each
// keep a private `identity<T>`, because an instantiation carries its package's
// prefix (`tests/link/package_generic`); this is one package, so they clash.
//
// `anchor` is imported only to load the other module; the clash is between the
// two `identity` templates and not between anything this file names.
import { anchor } from "./wordings_generic";

const identity = <T>(x: T): T => x;

export const main = (): i32 => identity(1) + anchor();
```

```text
Generic function `identity` is also defined in tests/wordings/nl3010_generic_redeclared.ts; a function name must be unique across the program, and an instantiation is named after its template
```

## NL3022

The message of an error contains:

```text
…; a constructor or method is named after its class, so two classes that share a name anywhere in the program cannot both declare it, whether or not either is exported; rename one of the classes
```

**No program provokes it**: a member symbol carries its package's prefix, so only two same-named structs of one package share one; declaredStructs compares each with its own package's first and refuses the pair first, a declared class as NL3028 and an instantiation at its template as NL3013, and skips their members (#193)

## NL3028

The message of an error contains:

```text
…; a class or interface name must be unique across the program whether or not it is exported, because a struct type is identified by its name alone
```

[`nl3028_class_name_clash.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl3028_class_name_clash.ts):

```ts
// NL3028: this module and `nl3_clash/lib.ts` each declare a class `Base`. A
// struct type is identified by its name alone, so the two would be one type;
// the later declaration in load order, `lib.ts`'s, is refused (#193). The two
// also share `Base.constructor`, which is not reported a second time.
import { anchor } from "./nl3_clash/lib";

class Base {
  x: i32 = 0;

  constructor(x: i32) {
    this.x = x;
  }
}

export const main = (): i32 => new Base(anchor()).x;
```

```text
Class `Base` is also declared in tests/wordings/nl3028_class_name_clash.ts; a class or interface name must be unique across the program whether or not it is exported, because a struct type is identified by its name alone
```

## NL3055

The message of an error contains:

```text
…` besides: Node copies every own field of the instance a value holds, and the native copy only the interface's, so spread a value of a class type, or set the fields by name
```

[`nl3055_object_spread_width.ts`](https://github.com/amritk/nish/blob/main/tests/wordings/nl3055_object_spread_width.ts):

```ts
// NL3055: A value of an interface type may hold a class instance with more fields; Node
// copies all of them and the native copy only the interface's, so a spread of
// such an interface is refused.
interface Named {
  name: i32;
}

interface Tagged {
  name: i32;
  tag: i32;
}

class Item implements Named {
  name: i32 = 1;
  weight: i32 = 2;
}

export const tag = (n: Named): i32 => {
  const t: Tagged = { ...n, tag: 3 };
  return t.tag;
};

export const main = (): i32 => tag(new Item());
```

```text
Spread of `Named` into `Tagged` may spread an instance of `Item`, which implements it with field `weight` besides: Node copies every own field of the instance a value holds, and the native copy only the interface's, so spread a value of a class type, or set the fields by name
```
